statement: OUR MOTHER MARYAM (OMM) is a UNIFIED DATE/TIME STANDARD.
note: A static file cannot tick on its own. Readers should compute live values with the rule below, or with omm-now.js. Historical calendar layers packaged with the clock page are research readings, not official religious or church doctrine. The epoch is marked provisional in the source v2 clock.

epoch.description: 1 May, astronomical year 0 (equal to 1 BCE), 00:00 UTC, proleptic Gregorian calendar. Python's datetime cannot represent year 0; the same instant is 245 days before 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z.
epoch.leap_seconds: none; every day is 86,400 SI-scale seconds as in Unix time
epoch.status: provisional, as marked in the source v2 grain clock

computation.rule: N = floor((unix_milliseconds - origin_unix_milliseconds) * 120 / 1000). Equivalently, at a whole Unix second, N = (unix_seconds - origin_unix_seconds) * 120.
computation.integer_arithmetic: Use integer (or BigInt) math. Do not multiply the millisecond offset by 120 in IEEE-754 binary64 if the product would exceed 2^53 − 1 (that overflow is still in the future, around year 2379).
computation.euclidean_decomposition: N = cowrie_index * 3,600,000 + grains * 120 + ticks, with cowrie_index = floor(N / 3,600,000), 0 ≤ grains < 30,000, and 0 ≤ ticks < 120.
computation.sign: N is 0 at the epoch, positive after it, and negative before it.

verified_snapshot.note: Fixed snapshot used by the v2 grain clock (Mon 9 Nov 2026, 18:04 UTC / 1:04 PM EST). The page's engine and this file agree on this value.

example_current.note: Worked example at a chosen instant, not a live feed. Recompute from the clock's time for a live reading.
